text:
maya: Quick question — in staging private deploys we tightened NetPol to only allow model-runtime pods egress to the KMS proxy (10.12.0.8:443). Our audit-forwarder (10.12.1.5:9200) is now getting dropped and alerts aren't showing up. Has anyone seen agent telemetry blocked like this?

sam: Can you paste the NetPolicy and the exact dropped log? also which CNI (calico/antrea)?

maya: calico. netpol snippet below — basically deny egress except kms-proxy.
```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: runtime-egress-lockdown
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: model-runtime
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 10.12.0.8/32 # kms-proxy
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 443
```

olivia: That policy looks right for KMS flows, but telemetry -> collector is a separate egress path. If the agent sends logs directly to the collector IP, netpol will block it unless you add an allow rule for the collector or proxy the telemetry through the kms-proxy/egress-proxy.

ops-dan: Two common approaches: (1) add a specific egress allow to 10.12.1.5:9200 with strict port restriction, or (2) run an egress-sidecar that forwards to collector over mTLS so the pod only talks to localhost. Both keep the model-runtime pod minimal.

sam: Is there any reason we don't want the runtime to talk to the collector IP directly? perf? security?

olivia: Main reason is isolation and minimizing blast radius. If the collector has more permissive upstream egress, we prefer telemetry to be push-only via a hardened proxy. Also KMS integration: agent uses the same proxy for key calls and we need audit logs to show via the same path for correlation.

maya: paste from calico felix: `IP ip-10-12-0-34 denied egress to 10.12.1.5 tcp/9200 (netpol runtime-egress-lockdown)` — that's the symptom.

sec-bot: :warning: observability-regression detected — telemetry egress blocked by networkpolicy runtime-egress-lockdown in namespace private-staging. Ticket: SEC-2026-014.

ops-dan: Workaround I pushed: added a rule above the deny to allow 10.12.1.5:9200 for pods with `app: model-runtime` and scoped by namespace. Example: `egress: - to: - ipBlock: { cidr: 10.12.1.5/32 } ports: - protocol: TCP port: 9200`. We should avoid wide CIDRs.

sam: Could we instead add a small proxy sidecar image and a Service for 127.0.0.1:9200 so NetPol only allows localhost? That decouples collector trust boundary.

olivia: Agree sidecar is cleaner for long-term. Action items: (a) ops to add scoped allow rule to unblock staging (b) infra to prototype egress-sidecar pattern with mTLS and audit headers (c) product/sec to update runbook to include telemetry allow when hardening NetPol.

maya: +1. I'll add the allow for staging and open a PR for sidecar prototype. I'll also attach packet capture and felix logs to the ticket.

ops-dan: Note: when you add allow rules, also check DNS. Calico egress for FQDNs uses egress policy with DNS; if agent resolves collector via internal name you might need a rule or hard-code IP.

olivia: And for KMS integration: make sure the proxy preserves original client identity headers so audit logs can link key usage and model requests. We'll add a test that simulates stolen pod creds and confirms telemetry still contains pod id.

maya: thanks all — will follow up in SEC-2026-014 with links. :thumbsup:
